diagnoses.summary: pe-uk 2.132.6 has no Growth Plan SDLT relief: its 2024-25 schedule already equals the pre-relief world, so removing the relief changes nothing. The relief was law from 23 September 2022 to 31 March 2025.
The relief ended on 31 March 2025, so modern law from 2025-26 is the pre-relief world. The OBR's later costings of the increase are offset by its separate 'ending the Growth Plan change' measure.
The counterfactual keeps the relief from 2025-26, the first year the measure changes; the OBR's 2024-25 yield is timing around the end date, which an annual construction does not express.

diagnoses.evidence: pe-uk 2.143.0 variables/gov/hmrc/income_tax/allowances/{trading_allowance_deduction,property_allowance_deduction_if_used}.py; microcosm_uk_2024_25.h5 has no self_employment_gross_receipts column
diagnoses.summary: Without gross receipts, pe-uk relieves only profits within the £1,000 allowance and treats a larger profit as already reflecting the better of expenses and the allowance (trading_allowance_deduction, property_allowance_deduction_if_used). The Microcosm UK 2024-25 cut carries no self_employment_gross_receipts, so the partial-relief leg the OBR costed has nothing to act on, and most fully relieved profits fall within the personal allowance anyway. The removal is 0.20 of the scaled OBR costing.

From policyengine-uk 2.134.1 (52030637b, fixing #2238) additional-dwelling and non-residential purchase prices are inputs, nil unless the dataset imputes them; before, every home buyer's whole stock of other residential property was charged as one additional-dwelling purchase. The interim Microcosm cut was built for 2.132.6 and does not supply the inputs, so on 2.143.0 no household buys an additional dwelling: modern-law SDLT falls from £15.0bn to £8.1bn in 2025-26 and the surcharge has nothing to act on. Microcosm imputes both from microcosm#1308 (the property_purchases stage), so the pre-Budget cut carries them. A model swap is valid only where the data carries the newer model's inputs.

Both sides of this change come from one model fix. 2.132.6 charges every home buyer's whole stock of other residential property at the higher rates (policyengine-uk#2238), and its scale lacks Autumn Budget 2024's further 2pp, so its £0.94bn is a 1pp removal on an overstated base. 2.143.0 has the full scale but takes the additional-dwelling purchase as a dataset input, which the interim cut does not supply, so it returns 0. Neither number is the surcharge's yield; the pre-Budget cut imputes the purchases (microcosm#1308).
